author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I am willing to accept a manual drift check performed consistently every day during the promotion cycle. This is the only substitute for reliable signal I will tolerate if the automated stack remains unfunded. I will not accept a sporadic or ad hoc review as a valid replacement. The cost of flying blind during a promotion week is too high to ignore. I am prepared to give up the convenience of automated alerts to keep the process alive, provided the human review is rigorous and daily. This is my final position on the matter.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up the convenience of automated alerts in exchange for a consistent manual process, defining a specific concession they are prepared to make.
